items.title: Move Andhra Pradesh HC: Delhi High Court rejects PIL against closure of old Visakhapatnam airport
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday rejected a public interest litigation (PIL) petition challenging the closure of Visakhapatnam airport at Dega after commercial operations were transferred to the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia asked the petitioner, Gopala Krishna Kosaraju, to agitate his grievance before the Andhra Pradesh High Court. The Bench said that since the dominant cause of action arose in Andhra Pradesh, the petitioner must approach the jurisdictional High Court. "Petition dismissed on the ground of forum convenience. It is needless to say that the petitioner will be at liberty to agitate his case before the jurisdictional High Court," the Court ordered. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The old Visakhapatnam airport at INS Dega, which had handled scheduled commercial flights for decades, ceased such operations last month. The shutdown followed the inauguration of the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram on August 1. items.title: From a school canteen row to street violence: How Ahmedabad’s Malala controversy escalated
items.summary: “They beat us with iron and wooden rods. They hit my head, back and elbow even though we were trying to have a dialogue with them,” said Savan Zalariya, a theatre artiste and professor of political theatre at Ahmedabad University, about a book-reading session disrupted on August 27. The “silent reading session” organised by the Students and Youth Collective, Ahmedabad (SYCA), at AUDA Garden in Vastrapur had turned into a confrontation after a group of people allegedly associated with the Bajrang Dal and Vishva Hindu Parishad arrived at the venue, raised slogans, made communal remarks and assaulted participants. The group tore copies of I Am Malala by Malala Yousafzai and The Diary of a Young Girl by Anne Frank that participants had been reading. It turned violent, with several participants allegedly beaten with sticks and rods, according to SYCA members. The reading session had been organised in solidarity with a school in Ahmedabad that had faced objections over the inclusion of the two books in its reading programme. items.title: Driving at high speed alone not rash or negligent driving: Delhi High Court
items.summary: Vehicles are intended to be driven fast and the fact that a vehicle was moving at high speed does not, by itself, establish criminal rashness or negligence on the part of the driver, the Delhi High Court recently observed [State v Sanjay] . Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha made the observation while dismissing the Delhi government’s appeal against the acquittal of a tempo driver booked under Sections 279 (rash driving) and 304A (causing death by negligence) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for causing a woman’s death in a road accident in 2009. “ Vehicles are intended to be driven in speed. Merely because the vehicle was driven at high speed would not mean that the driver was rash or negligent by itself. ‘High speed’ or ‘over speed’ are relative terms, ” the Court said. items.title: Kerala's Muslim Women Fiercely Reject Grand Mufti's Decree to Stay Off Public Stages | Shortcut
items.summary: Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar, the Grand Mufti of India, made public statements at a conference in Kochi, saying that women shouldn't share public and religious spaces with unrelated men, in defense to a circular that barred women from public stages at religious events. He said their presence there could cause "great destruction." However, Malayalam news channels have been flooded with clips of Muslim women pushing back, and they've not held back. Kerala Women and Child Development Minister Bindhu Krishna said women have the same rights as men and stressed that religious beliefs must be respected alongside the Constitution.
